rows.basis: Line names one option plainly: a law letting full-time yeshiva students keep studying with no criminal or financial penalties; nothing else held (rule 3)
Line names one option plainly: require everyone to serve, exemptions only for a limited number of outstanding Torah scholars, cut benefits for refusers; nothing else held (rule 3)

Line names one option plainly: gradual enlistment through agreement with Haredi leadership, "based on her 2026 statements and her party's support for the coalition draft bill"; the 2014 vote is "dated background only" and names no option (rule 3)
"Tentative": the mapping "rests on indirect evidence", a July 2026 statement about Arab youth and not Haredim specifically (rule 2)

First option stated plainly: every 18-year-old serves, benefits tied to service (rule 3). gradual-targets-by-agreement is named only as the 2022 government bill that "his positions since 2024 have moved away from", so it is not held (rule 7)

Line names one option plainly: require everyone to serve, with sanctions on refusers (rule 3). Caveat: Bennett rejects any exemption quota, so the position "is stricter than this option's allowance for a small number of Torah scholars" (rule 8)
Line names one option plainly: a law letting full-time yeshiva students keep studying instead of serving, with no criminal or financial penalties; nothing else held (rule 3)

First option stated plainly (exemption law without sanctions); the party "has pragmatically accepted bills with gradual targets" for men not in full-time study, "but only while protecting full-time students" (rule 5)

"Mixed": the call for non-studying Haredim to enlist through dialogue "fits" gradual targets by agreement; the list leader's "enlistment, but not coercion" with incentives "also points toward" voluntary service (rule 5)

"Tentative": the mapping "rests on indirect evidence", an April 2026 statement by Hadash's main component against linking voting rights to military service; no Hadash statement on Haredi service was found (rule 2)

First option stated plainly (gradual entry through suited tracks and incentives); the party "also holds the exemption-protection element" of the anchor option for full-time students; "the evidence is mixed between these two options" (rule 5). Caveat: "without that option's funding cuts when targets are missed" (rule 8). Universal service with sanctions is "not propose[d]" (rule 7)

First option stated plainly (every 18-year-old serves, benefits tied to service); Haskel's trial period without sanctions and border yeshivas "partly resemble" gradual targets (rule 5). She "rules out a blanket exemption law", so the anchor option is not held (rule 7)

"The evidence is mixed": agreement with rabbis and suited frameworks is "closest to" gradual enlistment by agreement; the statement against coercion "also partly matches" voluntary service (rule 5). Caveats: no source shows support for enlistment targets or funding cuts, and the anti-coercion statement was not applied to service in general (rule 8)

First option stated plainly (gradual targets agreed with Haredi leaders, limited and phased sanctions); the arrest freeze and Torah-study basic law "also lean towards" the anchor option; "the evidence is mixed" (rule 5). Netanyahu's campaign statements "lean the other way" but the line names no option for them
"Tentative": the mapping "rests on those votes alone" (January 2022 coalition votes); no later Meretz position was found (rule 2)

Line sets the "stated position" (gradual enlistment by agreement) against the 2025-2026 votes that protected yeshiva students from enforcement, "closer in practice to" the anchor option; "the evidence is mixed". Actions rank above statements, so the option backed by votes is first and the stated one second (rule 5 with the evidence ranking)
Line names one option plainly: compulsory service for all, a small number of Torah-scholar exemptions, loss of benefits for refusers; "this matches the platform closely" (rule 3)

"The evidence is mixed": Sa'ar's 2024 statements are closest to universal service with sanctions; the faction's 2026 votes are "closer to" the anchor option, and "the more recent actions carry more weight". Actions first, statements second (rule 5 with the evidence ranking)
"Tentative": the mapping "rests on indirect evidence", Ra'am's January 2022 votes as a coalition member; the party has not stated a current position (rule 2)

Line names one option plainly: a law letting full-time yeshiva students keep studying with no criminal or financial penalties (rule 3). Caveat: the party has accepted that men who leave yeshiva may be drafted under conditions suited to a Haredi lifestyle; the line names no second option for this (rule 8)

"Tentative": the mapping "rests on indirect evidence", Tibi calling the dispute an internal Jewish matter and supporting exemptions on grounds of conscience; no Ta'al position on Haredi service was found (rule 2)

Line names one option plainly: every 18-year-old serves, with consequences for refusers (rule 3). Caveat: the platform's sanctions "are aimed at institutions and their funding rather than at individuals" (rule 8)

Line names one option plainly: every 18-year-old serves, exemptions only for a small number of outstanding Torah scholars, loss of benefits for refusers (rule 3). Caveat: the proposed sanctions "go further than that option, including loss of the right to vote" (rule 8)
Line names one option plainly: require everyone to serve, a small quota of Torah scholars, loss of benefits for refusers; nothing else held (rule 3)

First option stated plainly: everyone must serve and those who don't lose state benefits; "this rests on the party's votes and platform since 2024" (rule 3). gradual-targets-by-agreement is named only as the approach of its January 2022 bill in government, which the line does not rest on, so it is not held (rule 7)

Line names one option plainly: require everyone to serve, benefits cut for refusers, supported by his votes and the joint list's plan (rule 3). Caveat: Tropper opposes criminal penalties, while the joint list's plan "goes further and adds criminal law" (rule 8)
Line names one option plainly: require every 18-year-old to serve in the army or civilian national service, with sanctions for refusers; nothing else held (rule 3)

Line names one option plainly: no forced long service, voluntary with incentives, resting on the 2026 platform (rule 3). Caveat: the platform "includes a short compulsory basic-training period for all" (rule 8). Feiglin's 2024 "need to enlist" statement "sits alongside it" with no option named; the 2013 and 2014 votes are "dated background only"
